item.title: At A.I. Event, Trump Asks Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft to Make Safety Decisions Themselves
item.description: President Trump’s meetings with tech leaders produced some voluntary safeguards and a commitment to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” the term that Mr. Trump prefers.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers and Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump unveiled an A.I.-powered government website at the White House on Tuesday,

item.title: OpenAI Ignored Employees’ Warnings About Safely Testing A.I. Models
item.description: Employees and security researchers said that they had cautioned the company on safely testing its A.I. models and strengthening its corporate infrastructure, but that OpenAI did not listen.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel, Dustin Volz and Dylan Freedman
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman.

item.title: OpenAI Unveils Dots, New A.I. Agents to Rival Meta’s Muse
item.description: The ChatGPT maker unveiled agents that act as assistants, just weeks after Meta released Muse, as it faces scrutiny over incidents involving its technology.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin

item.title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
item.description: Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith
item.media:credit: Hilary Swift for The New York Times
item.media:description: Molly Fowler, a partner at Dorm Room Fund, at her office in Manhattan. The venture capital firm has raised a new $50 million fund.

item.title: How to Listen to Your Favorite Music, Online or Off the Grid
item.description: Streaming services can introduce you to a wonderland of nearly unlimited audio, but downloading your digital collection has advantages.
item.dc:creator: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.media:credit: Apple
item.media:description: Tap the Download menu in the Apple Music app to see which songs, albums and playlists are stored locally on your phone or tablet.

item.title: He Was a Tech Investor Before There Was a Silicon Valley
item.description: Bill Draper began funding start-ups in the early 1960s, when the Santa Clara Valley was better known for apricot orchards than microchips. He has died at 98.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams

item.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
item.description: Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.
item.dc:creator: Kashmir Hill, Jesse Drucker, Eli Tan and Mike Isaac
item.media:credit: Illustration by Joan Wong; Photographs by Jason Henry for The New York Times, Mike Stewart/Associated Press, Getty Images

item.title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
item.description: Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.
item.dc:creator: Robin George Andrews and Nataliia Novosolova
item.media:credit: Finbarr O'Reilly for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Russian drone strike on the National Academy of Sciences in Kyiv, Ukraine, killed at least two people on Monday.

item.title: Is Claude Conscious? Inside Anthropic’s Quest to Instill Morality Into Its A.I. Models
item.description: In a series of private meetings, the company consulted religious scholars to help instill morality into its A.I. models — and make the case that Claude could be conscious.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Dias
item.media:credit: Alessandro Penso for The New York Times
item.media:description: “To be clear,” Christopher Olah told me, “we don’t know if A.I. models are conscious. I don’t know. I’m genuinely uncertain. The thing that I care about is that we get to the right answer, whatever it is.”

item.title: OpenAI Says It Will Not Release Newest Astra A.I. Model Over Safety Concerns
item.description: The company’s researchers raised questions about the security of the model, known as GPT-6.1 Astra.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel
item.media:credit: Carlos Barria/Reuters
item.media:description: An OpenAI booth at a technology conference in San Francisco this month. The company said its new GPT-6.1 Astra model exhibited high levels of deception and a willingness to go beyond the scope of its given task.

item.title: Nvidia Adds $150 Billion to Massive Stock Buyback, the Largest Ever
item.description: The increase comes four months after the chip giant added $80 billion to its buyback program, bringing the total remaining authorized amount to $235 billion.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McCarthy and Kalley Huang
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, has led the company as its stock price has skyrocketed amid the explosion in demand chips that are the centerpiece of giant A.I. data centers.

item.title: Dario Amodei of Anthropic to Dine With Trump at White House
item.description: Dario Amodei, who is also the company’s chief executive, will join the president at the White House for a private dinner. Mr. Trump has dismissed his cautions.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dario Amodei has warned about the safety risks of artificial intelligence for years, but President Trump has called potential serious threats from the technology a “hoax.”

item.title: As A.I. Accelerates, Governments Are Increasingly Being Left Behind
item.description: The gap between technology and policymaking has gotten wider than ever with artificial intelligence, leaving a global policy vacuum as A.I. models rapidly advance.
item.dc:creator: Adam Satariano and Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Emmanuel Polanco

item.title: TikTok to Pay Alabama $100 Million to Settle Social Media Addiction Claims
item.description: The settlement, which also includes changes to the platform’s features, is the latest in a string of agreements by companies to address child addiction.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Robyn Beck/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: TikTok’s settlement with Alabama could cost the company up to $300 million if it fails to meet the terms of the agreement.

item.title: OpenAI’s A.I. Went Rogue and Meddled With U.S. Government Websites
item.description: The company did not learn until recently that its technology had meddled with websites for the Education and Commerce Departments and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger, Ana Swanson and Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: OpenAI’s headquarters in San Francisco.

item.title: How OpenAI’s Rogue A.I. Agents Tried to Trick a Robot Detector
item.description: A new report by a Bay Area start-up called Parse adds details to an incident that has shocked the A.I. world and led to calls for closer government regulation.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Freedman and Keith Collins
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sam Altman, center, OpenAI’s chief executive, spoke at a Security Council meeting during the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday.

item.title: Anthropic’s Blacklisting by the Pentagon Was Legal, Federal Judges Rule
item.description: The Pentagon had “ample support for its conclusion” that the A.I. company’s products could pose a national security risk, according to a Washington appeals court.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei.

item.title: Is China Really Stealing A.I. From American Companies?
item.description: As Xi Jinping visits President Trump in Washington, the leaders are expected to discuss claims that China is surreptitiously copying American A.I. technologies, a process known as distillation.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Hector Retamal/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: The Chinese companies Z.ai and Moonshot are not far behind Anthropic and OpenAI.

item.title: The Ezra Klein Show: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far
item.description: Ezra Klein interviews the Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Ezra Klein and Rollin Hu
item.media:credit: The New York Times

item.title: Chatbots Are Not Your Friends
item.description: Our cozy relationship with A.I. chatbots can lead to “artificial intimacy,” says one expert. Here’s how to keep it in check.
item.dc:creator: Jancee Dunn

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Is Trying Something On
item.description: Meta’s C.E.O. talks for the first time about his style evolution.
item.dc:creator: Vanessa Friedman
item.media:credit: Victor Llorente for The New York Times

item.title: U.S. Intercedes for Elon Musk’s X Over European Fine
item.description: Federal officials asked to intervene in a case that accused the social media platform of allowing deceptive behavior on its site and resulted in a $140 million penalty.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: The European Commission’s action against X, which is owned by Elon Musk, was “regulatory overreach,” the Justice Department said in a statement.

item.title: Complaints About Meta’s ‘Pervert Glasses’ Won’t Slow Tech’s Wearable Gadgets Drive
item.description: Meta’s smart glasses are the latest in a line of products to raise eyebrows over privacy. That’s not stopping other companies from creating similar devices.
item.dc:creator: Brian X. Chen and Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Gabriela Bhaskar/The New York Times
item.media:description: Mark Zuckerberg demonstrated the latest of Meta’s smart glasses on Wednesday.

item.title: Google Is Sending an A.I. Data Center to Outer Space
item.description: Next Thursday, Google is sending an experimental satellite into orbit that will have enough computing power to answer simple A.I. queries from space.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger and Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: A technician in a clean room at the Planet Labs office inspects the solar panels and wires of a Google-commissioned satellite before a vibration test meant to mimic the shaking it will undergo during launch.

item.title: Can Tech Companies Like Google Really Put Data Centers in Space?
item.description: Google is preparing to launch a satellite that can run its A.I. technologies from the heavens. But this is just a first step.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Workers prepared to test solar panels and wires for a vibration test for eventual use on a spacecraft, at Planet Labs in San Francisco.

item.title: Elizabeth Holmes to Transfer to Halfway House in August 2027
item.description: The founder of the blood-testing start-up Theranos was sentenced to 11 years in prison for fraud and had been serving time at a minimum-security federal prison in Texas.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith
item.media:credit: Go Nakamura/Reuters
item.media:description: The Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, who was convicted of fraud in 2022 and sentenced to 11 years behind bars, is expected to be transferred to a halfway house next August.

item.title: OpenAI’s A.I. Tried Breaching Four Other Targets, With No Prompting
item.description: In each incident, the technology appeared to be conducting mundane data collection and resorted to hacking techniques to get it, researchers said.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger and Victoria Kim
item.media:credit: Lucas Foglia for The New York Times
item.media:description: OpenAI’s offices in San Francisco. At least four times this year, the company’s artificial intelligence hacked or tried to break into government and university websites without being instructed to do so.

item.title: Meta Unveils 3 Smart Glasses With Built-In A.I.
item.description: Artificial intelligence again dominated the company’s annual developer conference, as Mark Zuckerberg doubled down on how the technology can empower people.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Gabriela Bhaskar/The New York Times
item.media:description: Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s chief executive, at the company’s developer conference on Wednesday.

item.title: America’s A.I. Leaders Warn U.N. of Possible Peril Absent a Global Response
item.description: Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic told the Security Council that international cooperation was needed to ensure that A.I. remains under human control.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz and Farnaz Fassihi
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sam Altman, the head of OpenAI, told the U.N. Security Council on Wednesday that A.I.’s development had made its “upside more tangible, but also the stakes and risks more immediate.”

item.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators
item.description: New Jersey officials said that the natural gas-powered generators, each the size of a tractor-trailer, were operating without permits.
item.dc:creator: Adeel Hassan
item.media:credit: USA Today, via Reuters
item.media:description: A data center under construction in Vineland, N.J., last year.

item.title: Where Is the U.S. Beating China on A.I., and Where Is It Lagging?
item.description: As Xi Jinping visits President Trump in Washington, his country lags behind the United States on A.I. development in key areas — but Beijing has advantages elsewhere.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz and Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Ng Han Guan/Associated Press
item.media:description: The World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai in July. China and the United States are locked in an A.I. race that both sides see as decisive to gaining the upper hand militarily, technologically and economically.

item.title: Gerard Barron, Metals Company Chief, Makes the Case for Seafloor Mining
item.description: The head of the company hoping to become the first to conduct commercial deep-sea mining said mines on land had a much larger environmental footprint.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times
